alabama.sc_text: You have 14 days from the judgment to appeal to the circuit court. The circuit court hears the case all over again — a trial de novo — so you can bring your evidence and witnesses again. You must post a bond or other security for costs, or file an affidavit of substantial hardship if you cannot afford it. (Ala. Code § 12-12-70(a); Alabama Small Claims Rule M.)
alabama.sc_link_label: Alabama Small Claims Rules | Alabama Judicial System
alabama.gen_court: Alabama Court of Civil Appeals (most civil cases) or the Alabama Supreme Court
alabama.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 42 days (6 weeks) from entry of the judgment to file a notice of appeal with the clerk of the trial court. The appeal goes to the Alabama Court of Civil Appeals in most civil cases, or to the Alabama Supreme Court. The higher court reviews the record for legal errors — it does not hear new evidence. (Alabama Rules of Appellate Procedure, Rule 4.)
alabama.gen_link_label: Alabama Rules of Appellate Procedure, Rule 4 | Alabama Judicial System

alaska.sc_text: You have 30 days from the date shown on the clerk's certificate of distribution to appeal to the superior court. The superior court reviews the record — the recording, the evidence, and the file — and does not take new evidence. The filing fee is $100, plus a $750 cost bond, unless you ask the court to waive or reduce the bond or to accept a supersedeas bond instead. (Alaska Appellate Rule 602; District Court Rule of Civil Procedure 18.)
alaska.sc_link_label: Alaska Appellate Rules 601–612 (SCO 1015) | Alaska Court System
alaska.sc_link2_label: AP-200: Instructions for Appealing a Small Claims Case | Alaska Court System
alaska.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days from the date shown on the clerk's certificate of distribution to file a notice of appeal to the Alaska Supreme Court. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (Alaska Appellate Rule 204.)
alaska.gen_link_label: Alaska Rules of Appellate Procedure, Rule 204 | Alaska Court System
alaska.afford_note: In Alaska, you can ask the court to waive or reduce the $750 cost bond, or to accept a supersedeas bond instead.

arizona.sc_text: There is no appeal from a small-claims judgment in Arizona. The decision is final and binding. (A.R.S. § 22-519.) The way to keep appeal rights is to move the case out of small claims before the hearing: either side may transfer the case to the justice court's regular civil division at least 10 business days before the hearing. (A.R.S. § 22-504.) In the regular civil division, either side may appeal to the superior court within 14 days, and the superior court reviews the record.
arizona.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after the ruling to file a notice of appeal at the superior court, and the case goes to the Arizona Court of Appeals. There is no new trial at the Court of Appeals and no new evidence or witnesses — the court reviews the record for legal errors. Miss the deadline and the Court of Appeals will dismiss the appeal.
arizona.gen_link_label: Civil Appeals — Appellant's Guide for Self-Represented Litigants | Arizona Court of Appeals, Division One

arkansas.sc_text: You have 30 days to appeal to the circuit court, and the circuit court hears the case all over again — a trial de novo. File with the clerk of the circuit court; the filing fee is $100. A bond may be required, and an appeal stays the judgment while it is pending. (Arkansas District Court Rules 9(a) and 2(b).)
arkansas.sc_link_label: Arkansas District Court Rules | Arkansas Courts
arkansas.gen_court: Arkansas Court of Appeals (or the Arkansas Supreme Court)
arkansas.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days from entry of the judgment to file a notice of appeal, and the case goes to the Arkansas Court of Appeals (or the Arkansas Supreme Court). The higher court reviews the record for legal errors. (Arkansas Rules of Appellate Procedure — Civil, Rule 4(a).)
arkansas.gen_link_label: Arkansas Rules of Appellate Procedure — Civil, Rule 4 | Arkansas Courts

california.sc_text: You have 30 days after the clerk mails the notice of entry of judgment to appeal to the superior court, which holds a new hearing — a trial de novo — before a different judicial officer. Only the defendant can appeal the plaintiff's claim, and only the plaintiff can appeal the defendant's counterclaim: if you filed the claim, you cannot appeal a judgment against you on your own claim. If you are the defendant and you did not appear, ask the court to vacate the judgment first; if that motion is denied, you have 10 days to appeal the denial. The judgment on appeal is final. (Code of Civil Procedure §§ 116.750(b), 116.770.)
california.sc_link_label: Post-Judgment Proceedings (Small Claims) | Solano Superior Court
california.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 60 days to file a notice of appeal — 60 days after the superior court clerk serves a notice of entry of judgment or a file-endorsed copy of the judgment, 60 days after a party serves or is served with such a document, or 180 days after entry of judgment, whichever is earliest. The case goes to the California Court of Appeal, which reviews the record for legal errors. (California Rules of Court, Rule 8.104.)
california.gen_link_label: California Rules of Court, Rule 8.104 — Time to appeal | Judicial Branch of California

colorado.sc_text: You have 14 days from entry of the judgment to file a notice of appeal and an appeal bond in the county court, and you must also file a notice in the district court within 35 days. The district court reviews the case on the papers only — no new evidence and no new hearing. The district-court appeal filing fee is $163; if you cannot afford it, ask the clerk about a fee waiver (forms JDF 205/206). (C.R.S. § 13-6-311; JDF 126.)
colorado.sc_link_label: JDF 126: Notice of Appeal (County Court) | Colorado Judicial Branch
colorado.gen_text: In other civil cases from the district court, you have 49 days from the final order (or from an order denying a timely motion for post-trial relief) to file a notice of appeal to the Colorado Court of Appeals. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (Colorado Judicial Branch Appeals Quick Guide.)
colorado.gen_link_label: Appeals Quick Guide | Colorado Judicial Branch
colorado.afford_note: In Colorado, ask the clerk about a fee waiver (forms JDF 205/206) if you cannot afford the $163 district-court appeal filing fee.

connecticut.sc_text: There is no appeal from a small-claims case in Connecticut. (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 52-263.) The only route after judgment is a motion to open the judgment, which must be filed within 4 months after the judgment was sent — and only for an error such as not having actual notice of the case. (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 52-212; Practice Book Rule 24-29.) Ask the clerk for the form the same week you learn of the judgment.
connecticut.sc_link_label: Connecticut General Statutes, Chapter 902 (Appeals) | Connecticut General Assembly
connecticut.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 20 days from the date notice of the judgment or decision is issued to file an appeal to the Connecticut Appellate Court. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (Connecticut Practice Book, § 63-1.)
connecticut.gen_link_label: Handbook of Connecticut Appellate Procedure | Connecticut State Library

delaware.sc_text: You have 15 days to appeal to the Court of Common Pleas, which hears the case all over again — a trial de novo. The filing fee is $125 plus a $10 court security fee ($135 total). You must also apply for a bond to stop enforcement of the judgment while the appeal is pending. Landlord/tenant possession cases follow a different route: a 3-judge Justice of the Peace panel, within 5 business days. (10 Del. C. § 9571.)
delaware.sc_link_label: Post-Judgment Procedures (Justice of the Peace Court) | Delaware Courts
delaware.sc_link2_label: Appeals from Justice of the Peace Court | Delaware Courts
delaware.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after entry of the judgment on the docket to file a notice of appeal with the Clerk of the Delaware Supreme Court. The Supreme Court reviews the record for legal errors. (Delaware Supreme Court Rule 6(a)(i).)
delaware.gen_link_label: Delaware Supreme Court Rule 6(a) | Delaware Courts

florida.sc_text: Either side has 30 days from rendition of the judgment to appeal to the circuit court. The circuit court reviews the record for legal errors only — it does not re-try the case or hear new evidence. If you want a new trial instead, you have 10 days to move for one. Ask the clerk for the current filing fee before you file. (Florida Rule of Appellate Procedure 9.110(b); Florida Small Claims Rule 7.230.)
florida.sc_link_label: Florida Small Claims Rules (Jan. 1, 2026) | The Florida Bar
florida.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days from rendition of the final order to file a notice of appeal, with any filing fees, with the clerk of the lower court. The case goes to the District Court of Appeal, which reviews the record for legal errors. (Florida Rule of Appellate Procedure 9.110(b).)
florida.gen_link_label: Florida Rules of Appellate Procedure, Rule 9.110 | Fifth District Court of Appeal

georgia.sc_text: You have 30 days after the final judgment is filed or recorded to file a petition for review with the clerk of the state court or the superior court of the county. The reviewing court decides the case again — a de novo review. There is no appeal from a default judgment or from a dismissal for want of prosecution; those go by a petition for review of a denied motion to vacate. (O.C.G.A. §§ 15-10-41(b)(1), 5-3-7(b).)
georgia.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days from the final order to file a notice of appeal to the Georgia Court of Appeals. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (O.C.G.A. § 5-6-38.)
georgia.gen_link_label: Citizen's Guide to Direct Appeals | Georgia Court of Appeals

hawaii.sc_text: There is no appeal from a small-claims judgment in Hawaii. The decision is final. (HRS § 633-28.) Your only recourse after judgment is a motion to set aside the judgment, which must be filed within 10 days. Ask the clerk for the form right away — 10 days passes fast.
hawaii.sc_link_label: HRS Chapter 633 (Small Claims) | Hawaii State Legislature
hawaii.sc_link2_label: Small Claims Court Brochure | Hawaii State Judiciary
hawaii.gen_text: In other civil cases, when an appeal is permitted by law, you have 30 days after entry of the judgment or appealable order to file a notice of appeal. The case goes to the Hawaii Intermediate Court of Appeals, which reviews the record for legal errors. (Hawaii Rules of Appellate Procedure, Rule 4.)
hawaii.gen_link_label: Hawaii Rules of Appellate Procedure, Rule 4 | Hawaii State Judiciary

idaho.sc_text: You have 30 days to appeal to a lawyer magistrate or to the district court, and the appeal is a trial de novo — the case is tried all over again. The appeal fee is $20, unless it is waived. If you appeal and lose again, the other side may be awarded an attorney's fee. (Idaho Code § 1-2311; Idaho Rules of Small Claims Actions, Rule 15.)
idaho.sc_link_label: Idaho Code § 1-2311 (Small Claims Appeals) | Idaho Legislature
idaho.gen_court: Idaho Supreme Court (district court for magistrate judgments)
idaho.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 42 days from the date of the judgment to file a notice of appeal — 42 days to the district court from a magistrate court judgment, and 42 days to the Idaho Supreme Court from a district court judgment. The higher court reviews the record for legal errors.

illinois.sc_text: You have 30 days after entry of the final judgment to file a notice of appeal with the clerk of the circuit court — or 30 days after the order disposing of the last timely posttrial motion. Small claims are a division of the circuit court, so the appeal goes straight to the Illinois Appellate Court, which reviews the record for legal errors. Enforcement of the judgment is stayed only if you file a timely notice and an appeal bond or other security approved by the court. (Illinois Supreme Court Rules 303(a)(1), 305(a).)
illinois.sc_link_label: Illinois Supreme Court Rule 303 | Illinois Courts
illinois.gen_text: In other civil cases, the same 30-day rule applies: file the notice of appeal with the clerk of the circuit court within 30 days after entry of the final judgment, or within 30 days after the order disposing of the last timely posttrial motion. The case goes to the Illinois Appellate Court. (Illinois Supreme Court Rule 303(a)(1).)
illinois.gen_link_label: Illinois Supreme Court Rule 303 | Illinois Courts

indiana.sc_text: You have 30 days to appeal. Where the case goes depends on the court it started in: small claims in a circuit or superior court go to the Indiana Court of Appeals, which reviews the record — no new trial. In Marion County, township small-claims judgments entered after June 30, 2018 also go to the Court of Appeals on the record. Small claims in a city or town court go to the circuit court for a trial de novo, within 15 days — ask the clerk which route your case takes. (Indiana Small Claims Manual, 2026; IC § 33-34-3-15.1.)
indiana.sc_link_label: Indiana Small Claims Manual (2026) | Indiana Courts
indiana.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after the final judgment is noted on the trial court's Chronological Case Summary to file a notice of appeal to the Indiana Court of Appeals. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (Indiana Appellate Rule 9.)
indiana.gen_link_label: Appellate Clerk's Office FAQs | Indiana Courts

iowa.sc_text: You have 20 days to appeal to the district court. Give oral notice at the hearing, or file written notice within 20 days, and pay the district court docket fee within the same 20 days — no appeal may be taken after 20 days. The district court hears the appeal promptly on the record filed, without further evidence: this is a record review, not a new trial. Collection is stayed only if you post an appeal bond in the amount of the judgment. A transcript must be filed within 20 days. (Iowa Code § 631.13.)
iowa.sc_link_label: Iowa Code § 631.13 (Small Claims Appeals) | Iowa Legislature
iowa.gen_court: Iowa Supreme Court (usually through the Court of Appeals)
iowa.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after filing of the final order or judgment to file a notice of appeal in the district court, with an informational copy to the supreme court. The Iowa Supreme Court (usually through the Court of Appeals) reviews the record for legal errors. (Iowa Rule of Appellate Procedure 6.101.)
iowa.gen_link_label: Iowa Rules of Appellate Procedure, Rule 6.101 | Iowa Legislature

kansas.sc_text: You have 14 days after entry of the judgment to file a notice of appeal with the clerk of the district court. The appeal is tried all over again — a trial de novo — before a district judge. Enforcement of the judgment is automatically stayed while the appeal is pending; no supersedeas bond is required. If you cannot afford the appeal filing fee, ask the clerk about a poverty affidavit. (K.S.A. § 61-2709(a).)
kansas.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days from entry of the judgment to file a notice of appeal with the clerk of the district court. The case goes to the Kansas Court of Appeals, which reviews the record for legal errors. (K.S.A. § 60-2103.)
kansas.afford_note: In Kansas, a poverty affidavit can waive the appeal filing fee.

kentucky.sc_deadline: 10 days (notice); statement of appeal within 30 days
kentucky.sc_text: You have 10 days to file a notice of appeal to the circuit court, and then 30 days from filing the notice to file a statement of appeal. The circuit court hears the case de novo — retried, with the chance to present new evidence or arguments. (KRS § 24A.340.)
kentucky.sc_link_label: Kentucky Revised Statutes, Chapter 24A (District Court) | Justia
kentucky.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days from the date of notation of service of the judgment or order to file a notice of appeal with the clerk of the court the appeal is taken from. The case goes to the Kentucky Court of Appeals, which reviews the record for legal errors. (Kentucky Rule of Appellate Procedure 3.)
kentucky.gen_link_label: Kentucky Rules of Appellate Procedure, RAP 3 | Kentucky Court of Justice

louisiana.sc_text: You have 15 days to appeal from a justice of the peace court to the district or parish court, which tries the case de novo — all over again. There is no further appeal from the district or parish court's judgment. In city court, the plaintiff gives up the right to appeal by filing there; the defendant can preserve appeal rights by asking to transfer the case to the regular court within 10 days of receiving notice of the complaint. (La. Code of Civil Procedure art. 4925(A).)
louisiana.sc_link_label: La. Code of Civil Procedure art. 4925 | Louisiana Legislature
louisiana.sc_link2_label: A Guide to Louisiana Justice of the Peace Court | Louisiana Attorney General
louisiana.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 60 days to take a devolutive appeal — one that does not suspend enforcement of the judgment — counted from the expiration of the delay for applying for a new trial, if no application was filed. If you want the appeal to suspend enforcement, that suspensive appeal must be taken within 30 days. The case goes to the Louisiana Court of Appeal. (La. Code of Civil Procedure arts. 2087, 2123.)
louisiana.gen_link_label: La. Code of Civil Procedure art. 2087 | Louisiana Legislature

maine.sc_text: You have 30 days to appeal to the Superior Court. The two sides are treated differently: the plaintiff can appeal only on questions of law — the Superior Court reviews the record and needs a transcript — while the defendant can also ask for a new trial before a jury. Ask the clerk for the current appeal fee before you file. (Maine Rules of Small Claims Procedure, Rule 11.)
maine.gen_court: Maine Supreme Judicial Court (the Law Court)
maine.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 21 days after the court's entry of the judgment or order to file your appeal to the Maine Supreme Judicial Court (the Law Court). A late appeal will be dismissed. (Maine Judicial Branch, How To File a Civil Appeal, form CV-092.)
maine.gen_link_label: How To File a Civil Appeal (CV-092) | Maine Judicial Branch

maryland.sc_text: You have 30 days to appeal to the circuit court. A small claim — $5,000 or less — gets a new trial (de novo) in the circuit court. Cases over $5,000 are reviewed on the record instead. Total appeal fees are $175 ($10 to the District Court and $165 to the Circuit Court), plus a $75 transcript deposit; the judge may order a supersedeas bond to stop enforcement. Landlord/tenant cases are much shorter: 4 business days for failure to pay rent, 10 days for holdover or breach. (Md. Code, Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 12-401.)
maryland.sc_link_label: Appeals and Motions After Trial in the District Court | Maryland Courts
maryland.gen_court: Appellate Court of Maryland (circuit court for District Court cases)
maryland.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after the judgment date to file an appeal to the circuit court (from the District Court) or to the Appellate Court of Maryland (from the circuit court). The higher court reviews the record for legal errors — except small claims of $5,000 or less, which get a new trial. (Maryland Courts, Appeals and Motions After Trial in the District Court.)
maryland.gen_link_label: Appeals and Motions After Trial in the District Court | Maryland Courts

massachusetts.sc_text: The defendant has 10 days after receiving written notice of the magistrate's decision to appeal for a new trial before a judge or a jury of six. The plaintiff cannot appeal a judgment on the plaintiff's own claim — filing the claim waives that right — but the plaintiff can appeal the defendant's counterclaim. A defendant who defaulted cannot appeal, and there is no appeal if the defendant chose a judge trial at the start. The appeal fee is $25 (waivable if you are indigent), plus a $100 appeal bond or deposit, refundable if you win (also waivable if you cannot afford it and the appeal is not frivolous). There is no further appeal from the jury session. (Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 218, § 23.)
massachusetts.sc_link_label: Small Claims Standards: Appealing from the Judgment | Mass.gov
massachusetts.gen_deadline: 30 days (60 if the Commonwealth is a party)
massachusetts.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days from entry of the judgment to file a notice of appeal with the clerk of the lower court — 60 days if the Commonwealth or one of its officers or agencies is a party. The case goes to the Massachusetts Appeals Court, which reviews the record for legal errors. (Mass. Rules of Appellate Procedure, Rule 4.)
massachusetts.afford_note: In Massachusetts, the $25 appeal fee and the $100 bond can both be waived if you cannot afford them and the appeal is not frivolous.

michigan.sc_deadline: No appeal (7 days if a magistrate decided)
michigan.sc_text: Usually, there is no appeal from a small-claims judgment in Michigan: by staying in small claims, you waive the right to appeal if a district judge decided the case. (MCL § 600.8412.) The exception: if an attorney-magistrate decided the case, either side may appeal to a district judge for a new trial (de novo) within 7 days, with no fee — and the judge's decision is final, with no further appeal. (MCL § 600.8427.) To keep your options open, either side can ask for a judge instead of a magistrate before trial, or move the case to the general civil division before trial.
michigan.sc_link_label: MCL Chapter 600, Act 236, Chapter 84 (Small Claims) | Michigan Legislature
michigan.gen_court: Michigan Court of Appeals (circuit court for district court cases)
michigan.gen_text: In other civil cases, an appeal of right to the circuit court must be taken within 21 days after entry of the judgment, and an appeal from the circuit court to the Michigan Court of Appeals within 21 days after entry of the judgment. The higher court reviews the record for legal errors. (Michigan Court Rules, Chapter 7.)
michigan.gen_link_label: Michigan Court Rules, Chapter 7 | Michigan Courts

minnesota.sc_text: You have 21 days to appeal — not 60. Conciliation court (small claims) judgments are appealed by removal to the district court for a trial de novo: the case is tried all over again. File a demand for removal, an affidavit of good faith, and an affidavit of service within 21 days after the court administrator sends notice of the judgment order. If you remove the case and do not win in district court, the other side may be awarded an additional $50 in costs. The district court's decision can then be appealed to the Court of Appeals like any other civil case. Cases decided by default cannot be removed. (Minn. R. Gen. Pract. 521, effective July 1, 2026; Minn. Stat. § 491A.02, subds. 6–8.) Note: the 60-day figure printed in the Small Claims section on this page is the general civil appeal rule — it is not the conciliation-court deadline. Yours is 21 days.
minnesota.sc_link_label: Minn. R. Gen. Pract. 521 (Conciliation Court Appeals) | Minnesota Revisor
minnesota.sc_link2_label: Conciliation Court Handbook, Chapter 5 | Minnesota Attorney General
minnesota.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 60 days after entry of a judgment to appeal to the Minnesota Court of Appeals — and 60 days after service of written notice of filing for an appealable order. This 60-day rule is the general civil deadline; it does not apply to conciliation court, which is 21 days (see above). The Court of Appeals reviews the record for legal errors. (Minn. R. Civ. App. P. 103.03.)
minnesota.gen_link_label: Minnesota Rules of Civil Appellate Procedure | Minnesota Judicial Branch

mississippi.sc_text: You have 10 days after the judgment to demand an appeal and post bond. The appeal goes to the county court, if the county has one, or to the circuit court. The bond must be double the judgment (or double the value of the property involved), plus costs, and at least $100, with a surety approved by the justice court clerk. Once demanded and bonded, the appeal pauses enforcement of the judgment. If you cannot afford the bond, you can still appeal by filing a poverty affidavit — but then the judgment is not paused. Ask the clerk whether the higher court retries the case or reviews the record; the statute does not say. (Miss. Code § 11-51-85.)
mississippi.gen_court: Mississippi Supreme Court (usually assigned to the Court of Appeals)
mississippi.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after entry of the judgment or order to file a notice of appeal, and it must be received and filed with the lower court clerk within that time. The case goes to the Mississippi Supreme Court (usually assigned to the Court of Appeals), which reviews the record for legal errors.
mississippi.gen_link_label: Clerk of Appellate Court General Information | Mississippi Judiciary
mississippi.afford_note: In Mississippi, a defendant who cannot afford the bond can still appeal by filing a poverty affidavit — but the judgment is not paused while the appeal is pending.

missouri.sc_text: You have 10 days after the judgment to file an application for a trial de novo with the small claims clerk. The case is then tried all over again before an associate circuit judge. The clerk mails a copy to the other side within 15 days. Consent judgments cannot be appealed this way. Collection is not paused unless you post a recognizance (bond) with solvent sureties within the same 10 days. Ask the clerk for the current fee. (RSMo § 482.365.)
missouri.gen_deadline: 10 days after the judgment becomes final
missouri.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 10 days after the judgment becomes final to file a notice of appeal with the clerk of the trial court. The case goes to the Missouri Court of Appeals, which reviews the record for legal errors. (Missouri Supreme Court Rule 81.04.)
missouri.gen_link_label: Rule 81.04 (Appeals, When and How Taken) | Missouri Courts

montana.sc_text: You have 10 days from the original judgment to file a written appeal to the district court. The district court decides questions of law only — it does not retry the case or accept new evidence. Ask the clerk for the current fee. (Montana Department of Justice, Small Claims Court.) Note: the 30-day deadline you may see elsewhere is for general civil appeals from justice court, not small claims.
montana.sc_link_label: Small Claims Court | Montana Department of Justice
montana.gen_deadline: 30 days (60 if the U.S. is a party)
montana.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days from entry of the judgment to file a notice of appeal with the clerk of the supreme court — 60 days if the United States, the State of Montana, a political subdivision, or one of their officers or agencies is a party. The Montana Supreme Court reviews the record for legal errors. (Montana Rules of Appellate Procedure, Rule 4.)
montana.gen_link_label: Montana Rule of Appellate Procedure 4 | Montana Code Annotated

nebraska.sc_text: You have 30 days from entry of the judgment to file a notice of appeal and pay the district court docket fee, and within the same 30 days you must post a $50 cash bond or undertaking. The district court reviews the judgment for error appearing on the record — it does not hold a new trial. A supersedeas bond will stop collection while the appeal is pending. (Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 25-2729, 25-2733.)
nebraska.sc_link_label: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-2729 (Small Claims Appeals) | Nebraska Legislature
nebraska.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after entry of the judgment to file a notice of appeal in the office of the clerk of the district court. The case goes to the Nebraska Court of Appeals, which reviews the record for legal errors. (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-1912.)

nevada.sc_text: You have 7 calendar days from service of the judgment to file a notice of appeal — plus 3 more days if the judgment was served by mail. The appeal goes to the district court, which reviews the record; it does not hold a new trial, and there is no further appeal after the district court rules. The appeal cost bond is $115 and cannot be waived; the defendant must also post a bond for the judgment and interest. Ask the clerk for the current district court filing fee — it varies by county. (Nevada Justice Court Rules of Civil Procedure 98(b), 6(d), 100.)
nevada.sc_link_label: How to Appeal a Small Claims Judgment | Sparks Justice Court
nevada.sc_link2_label: Appealing a Small Claims Judgment | Clark County Civil Law Self-Help Center
nevada.gen_court: Nevada Supreme Court (usually assigned to the Court of Appeals)
nevada.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days from written notice of entry of the judgment to file an appeal to the Nevada Supreme Court (usually assigned to the Court of Appeals). An appeal does not let you re-do the trial or submit new evidence — the court looks only at what was submitted to the trial court.
nevada.gen_link_label: How to Appeal | Nevada Self-Help Center
nevada.afford_note: In Nevada, the $115 appeal cost bond cannot be waived.

new-hampshire.sc_text: You have 30 days to appeal to the Superior Court — 30 days from rendition of the judgment or from the clerk's notice of it, whichever is later. Ask the clerk whether the Superior Court retries the case or reviews the record; the sources disagree and no official source settles it. (N.H. Rules of the Circuit Court — District Division, Rule 4.9.)
new-hampshire.sc_link_label: Small Claims | New Hampshire Judicial Branch
new-hampshire.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days from the date on the trial court clerk's written notice of a decision on the merits to file a notice of appeal to the New Hampshire Supreme Court — the state's only appellate court. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (N.H. Supreme Court Rule 7(1).)
new-hampshire.gen_link_label: New Hampshire Supreme Court | NH Judicial Branch

new-jersey.sc_court: Appellate Division of the Superior Court
new-jersey.sc_text: Either side has 45 days to appeal to the Appellate Division of the Superior Court. File a notice of appeal, a transcript request, and a case information statement with the Clerk of the Appellate Division within 45 days. The filing fee is $250, plus a $300 deposit with the clerk within 30 days of the notice (refunded if you win). A transcript is required — budget for the deposit, estimated at the cost of the transcript or $300 per trial day. A fee waiver is available if you cannot afford it. The Appellate Division reviews the record for legal errors only — no new trial, no new evidence. An appeal does not automatically stop enforcement: ask for a stay. (N.J. Court Rules; njcourts.gov.)
new-jersey.sc_link_label: Can I Appeal a Small Claims Court Decision? | NJ Courts
new-jersey.gen_court: Appellate Division of the Superior Court
new-jersey.gen_text: In other civil cases, you also have 45 days from entry of the final judgment to file an appeal to the Appellate Division of the Superior Court. The court reviews the record for legal errors.
new-jersey.gen_link_label: Guide to Completing Appeals Forms | NJ Courts
new-jersey.afford_note: In New Jersey, a fee waiver is available under Court Rule 1:5-6.

new-mexico.sc_text: You have 15 days after the judgment is filed in the magistrate court clerk's office to file a notice of appeal in the district court. The district court holds a trial de novo — the case is tried all over again. The district court filing fee for a civil appeal from magistrate court is $132; if you cannot afford it, ask the clerk about a free-process (indigency) application, Form 4-222. (NMSA § 35-13-1; NMRA Rules 1-072, 2-705.)
new-mexico.sc_link_label: Civil Appeal in District Court from a Magistrate Court Judgment | New Mexico Supreme Court
new-mexico.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days to appeal from the district court to the New Mexico Court of Appeals. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (NMSA § 39-3-2.)
new-mexico.afford_note: In New Mexico, ask the clerk about a free-process (indigency) application, Form 4-222.

new-york.sc_text: You have 30 days to appeal to the County Court — 35 days if the judgment was served by mail. In New York City, the appeal goes to the Appellate Term. The higher court only decides whether substantial justice was done — whether the trial was basically fair — and will not change a small-claims decision over a technical mistake. By filing a small claim, the plaintiff gives up most appeal rights: either side may appeal only on substantial-justice grounds. There is no appeal from an arbitrator's decision (you have 35 days to ask for a new trial before a judge instead) and no appeal from a default judgment. Ask the clerk for the current fee. (Uniform Justice Court Act § 1807.)
new-york.sc_link_label: Uniform Justice Court Act § 1807 (Small Claims Appeals) | NY Senate
new-york.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after a party serves you with a copy of the judgment or order and written notice of its entry to take an appeal as of right to the Appellate Division. If you serve those documents yourself, your own 30 days run from that service. The Appellate Division reviews the record for legal errors. (CPLR § 5513(a).)
new-york.gen_link_label: Appeals in New York | Rosenhouse Law Office

north-carolina.sc_text: You have 10 days after the magistrate's decision to appeal for a trial de novo before a district court judge or a jury — the case is tried all over again. Give notice orally in open court, or file written notice with the clerk of superior court within 10 days. Costs are due within 20 days (10 days in summary ejectment cases), and an affidavit of indigency is due within 10 days if you cannot afford the costs. (N.C.G.S. § 7A-228.)
north-carolina.sc_link_label: N.C.G.S. § 7A-228 (Small Claims Appeals) | NC General Assembly
north-carolina.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days to file a notice of appeal to the North Carolina Court of Appeals. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (N.C. Rules of Appellate Procedure 3(c).)
north-carolina.gen_link_label: North Carolina Rules of Appellate Procedure, Rule 3 | NC Courts

north-dakota.sc_text: There is no appeal from a small-claims decision in North Dakota. The judge's or judicial referee's decision is final. The way to keep a fuller appeal is to move the case to district court before the hearing: the defendant may file a motion to remove the case within 20 days of service, using Form 3. Ask the clerk for the current removal fee.
north-dakota.sc_link_label: Small Claims Court Actions | North Dakota Court System
north-dakota.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 60 days from service of notice of entry of the judgment or order to file an appeal to the North Dakota Supreme Court. The court reviews the record for legal errors.
north-dakota.gen_link_label: North Dakota Court System — Document Return Request Form

ohio.sc_text: You have 30 days to appeal to the Court of Appeals, which reviews the record for questions of law — it does not re-try the case. If a magistrate decided the case, you must first file objections within 14 days of the filing of the magistrate's decision, supported by a transcript or affidavit; the 30 days to appeal then run from the order resolving the objections. If you do not object, you cannot argue the error on appeal except as plain error. (Ohio Appellate Rules 4(A), 4(B)(2); Ohio Civil Rule 53(D)(3)(b)(i).)
ohio.sc_link_label: Louden v. A.O. Smith Corp. (2009) — quotes Ohio App. R. 4(A) | Supreme Court of Ohio
ohio.gen_text: In other civil cases, the same 30-day rule applies: file a notice of appeal within 30 days of the later of entry of the judgment or, in a civil case, service of the notice of judgment and its entry if service was not made within the 3-day period in Civil Rule 58(B). The case goes to the Court of Appeals. (Ohio Appellate Rule 4(A).)
ohio.gen_link_label: Louden v. A.O. Smith Corp. (2009) — quotes Ohio App. R. 4(A) | Supreme Court of Ohio

oklahoma.sc_text: You have 30 days to appeal directly to the Oklahoma Supreme Court — small claims is already a docket of the district court, so there is no intermediate court. File a petition in error with the Clerk of the Supreme Court within 30 days after the judgment is filed with the trial court clerk. The Supreme Court reviews the record. Critical: a court reporter must have recorded the hearing, or there is no record and no appeal is possible — ask for a reporter (about $50) before or during the hearing. (12 O.S. §§ 1761, 990A.)
oklahoma.sc_link_label: 12 O.S. § 990A (Appeal to the Supreme Court) | Oklahoma State Courts Network
oklahoma.gen_text: In other civil cases, the same 30-day rule applies: file a petition in error with the Clerk of the Supreme Court within 30 days after the judgment is filed with the trial court clerk. (12 O.S. § 990A.)
oklahoma.gen_link_label: 12 O.S. § 990A (Appeal to the Supreme Court) | Oklahoma State Courts Network

oregon.sc_deadline: No appeal from circuit court; 10 days from justice court
oregon.sc_text: It depends on which court heard your case. Judgments from the small claims department of the circuit court cannot be appealed at all. (ORS § 46.485.) Judgments from a justice court small claims department can be appealed: the defendant (or the plaintiff, on a counterclaim) has 10 days after entry of the judgment to appeal to the circuit court for the county, where the case is tried without a jury. A bond is required, and there is no further appeal from the circuit court's judgment on the appeal. If you lose again, you owe the other side a $10 attorney's fee. (ORS §§ 55.110, 55.120.)
oregon.sc_link2_label: HB 2463 Staff Summary (Small Claims Appeals) | Oregon Legislature
oregon.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after the judgment is entered in the register to serve and file a notice of appeal to the Oregon Court of Appeals. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (ORS 19.255.)

pennsylvania.sc_text: You have 30 days after entry of the judgment to file a notice of appeal with the prothonotary of the Court of Common Pleas. The Common Pleas court hears the case de novo — all over again. Serve a copy of the notice on the other side and on the magisterial district judge within 10 days of filing. Landlord/tenant possession cases are shorter: 10 days (30 days if the tenant is a victim of domestic violence). (Pa.R.C.P.M.D.J. 1002.)
pennsylvania.sc_link_label: Pa.R.C.P.M.D.J. 1002 (Time and Method of Appeal) | Pennsylvania Code
pennsylvania.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after entry of the order to file a notice of appeal to the Pennsylvania Superior Court. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (Pa.R.A.P. 903(a).)
pennsylvania.gen_link_label: Pa.R.A.P. Chapter 9 (Appeals from Lower Courts) | Pennsylvania Code

rhode-island.sc_text: You have 2 days — the shortest small-claims appeal deadline in the country — to file a notice of appeal to the Superior Court, which holds a trial de novo. The 2 days do not count weekends and holidays; residential landlord/tenant cases get 5 days. Only the defendant may appeal a small-claims judgment: the plaintiff files a written waiver of appeal with the claim. Count the days the same day you get the judgment. (D.C.R. 73; R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 9-12-10, 10-16-14(a).)
rhode-island.sc_link_label: District Court Civil Rules (D.C.R. 73) | Rhode Island Courts
rhode-island.sc_link2_label: About the District Court | Rhode Island Courts
rhode-island.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 20 days from entry of the judgment to file a notice of appeal with the clerk of the trial court. The case goes to the Rhode Island Supreme Court, which reviews the record for legal errors. (R.I. Supreme Court Rules, Article I, Rule 4.)
rhode-island.gen_link_label: Rhode Island Supreme Court Rules, Article I, Rule 4 | Rhode Island Courts

south-carolina.sc_text: You have 30 days after delivery of written notice of the judgment — or 30 days from announcement of the judgment at trial — to file a notice of appeal to the circuit court (the Court of Common Pleas). The circuit court reviews the record; it does not hold a new trial. The magistrate files the return and the record within 30 days. A bond is typically required to stop collection while the appeal is pending. If you want a new trial instead, you have 10 days to move for one. Ask the clerk for the current filing fee. (S.C. Rules of Magistrates Court, Rule 18.)
south-carolina.sc_link_label: Magistrates Court Rule 18 (Appeals) | South Carolina Judicial Branch
south-carolina.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after receipt of written notice of entry of the order or judgment to serve a notice of appeal on all respondents. The case goes to the South Carolina Court of Appeals, which reviews the record for legal errors. (South Carolina Appellate Court Rule 203.)
south-carolina.gen_link_label: South Carolina Appellate Court Rule 203 | SC Judicial Branch

south-dakota.sc_text: There is no appeal from a small-claims decision in South Dakota. The ruling is final. (SDCL § 15-39-57.) The way to keep a fuller appeal is to ask to move the case to the regular civil docket before the hearing: the defendant may petition to remove the case at least 5 days before the appearance or answer date. Ask the clerk for the current removal fee.
south-dakota.sc_link_label: SDCL Chapter 16-12B (Small Claims) | South Dakota Legislature
south-dakota.sc_link2_label: SDCL § 15-39-57 (No Appeal from Small Claims) | LawServer
south-dakota.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after the judgment or order is signed, attested, filed, and written notice of entry is given to the adverse party to take an appeal to the South Dakota Supreme Court. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (SDCL 15-26A-6.)
south-dakota.gen_link_label: SDCL Chapter 15-26A (Civil Appellate Procedure) | South Dakota Legislature

tennessee.sc_text: Either side has 10 days to appeal from the general sessions court to the circuit court, and the circuit court hears the case de novo — from the beginning, as if the first hearing never happened. Before the appeal is granted you must give a bond with good security for the costs of the appeal, or take the oath for poor persons if you cannot afford it. If you want a jury trial in circuit court, ask within 10 days of filing the appeal. If no appeal is taken in time, execution on the judgment may issue. (Tenn. Code §§ 27-5-108, 27-5-103.)
tennessee.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after entry of the judgment to file a notice of appeal to the Tennessee Court of Appeals. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (Tennessee Rule of Appellate Procedure 4(a).)
tennessee.gen_link_label: Tennessee Rules of Appellate Procedure | Tennessee Courts
tennessee.afford_note: In Tennessee, you can take the oath for poor persons instead of posting a bond for the costs of the appeal.

texas.sc_text: You have 21 days after the judgment is signed — or after a motion to reinstate, set aside, or for a new trial is denied — to appeal from the justice court to the county court, which holds a trial de novo. You can appeal only if the judgment or the amount in dispute is more than $250, not counting court costs. Perfect the appeal with an appeal bond, a cash deposit, or a Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs, and pay the county court filing fee; once perfected, the justice court judgment is no longer valid or enforceable. The bond is $500 for a plaintiff and twice the judgment for a defendant. (Tex. R. Civ. P. 506.1.)
texas.sc_link_label: Appealing a Small Claims Case | Texas State Law Library
texas.gen_deadline: 30 days (90 with a timely post-judgment motion)
texas.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after the judgment is signed to file a notice of appeal to the Texas Court of Appeals — 90 days if a timely motion for a new trial or another listed post-judgment filing was made. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (Tex. R. App. P. 26.1.)
texas.gen_link_label: Texas Rules of Appellate Procedure | Texas Judicial Branch
texas.afford_note: In Texas, a Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs can take the place of an appeal bond or cash deposit.

utah.sc_text: Either side has 28 days from entry of the judgment to file a notice of appeal in the original trial court. The appeal goes to the district court of the county and is a trial de novo — tried all over again. The district court's decision on the new trial generally cannot be appealed further, unless the court ruled on the constitutionality of a statute or ordinance. (Utah Code § 78A-8-106.) Note: some older guides say 30 days; the current statute says 28.
utah.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after entry of the judgment to file a notice of appeal with the clerk of the trial court — 10 days for a judgment in a forcible entry or unlawful detainer action. The case goes to the Utah Court of Appeals, which reviews the record for legal errors. (Utah Rule of Appellate Procedure 4.)
utah.gen_link_label: Utah Rule of Appellate Procedure 4 | Utah Courts

vermont.sc_text: You have 30 days to appeal to the Superior Court. The appeal is heard and decided based on the record made in the small claims procedure — it is not a new trial. The filing fee was most recently listed at $120; confirm the current amount with the clerk before you file, because an older form lists $100. (12 V.S.A. § 5538.)
vermont.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days from entry of an appealable judgment to file a notice of appeal to the Vermont Supreme Court. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (12 V.S.A. § 2383.)

virginia.sc_text: You have 10 days to file a notice of appeal (Form DC-475) from the general district court to the circuit court, and you must perfect the appeal — post the bond and pay the writ tax — within 30 days. The circuit court hears the case de novo. Indigent defendants do not have to post a bond. (Va. Code §§ 16.1-106, 8.01-129.)
virginia.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days from the date of the final judgment to file a notice of appeal to the Virginia Court of Appeals. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (Va. Code § 8.01-675.3.)
virginia.gen_link_label: Va. Code § 8.01-675.3 | Virginia Legislative Information System
virginia.afford_note: In Virginia, indigent defendants do not have to post an appeal bond.

washington.sc_text: You have 30 days after the judgment is rendered to appeal from the district court to the superior court. File the notice of appeal in the district court, pay the statutory superior court filing fee, post a bond or undertaking, and serve all parties — all within the 30 days. There is no appeal unless the amount in controversy is more than $250. The superior court reviews the case 'de novo upon the record' — it re-decides the case from the record, without a new trial. A bond is required to stop enforcement while the appeal is pending. (RCW 12.36.020, 12.36.055(1), 12.36.010.)
washington.sc_link_label: RCW Chapter 12.36 (Small Claims Appeals) | Washington Legislature
washington.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days after entry of the decision to file a notice of appeal in the trial court. The case goes to the Washington Court of Appeals, which reviews the record for legal errors. (Washington Rule of Appellate Procedure 5.2(a).)

west-virginia.sc_text: You have 20 days after the judgment is entered — or 20 days after the magistrate denies a motion for a new trial — to file a notice of appeal in the magistrate court. The appeal goes to the circuit court. If the case was tried without a jury, the circuit court holds a trial de novo; if it was tried before a jury, the circuit court reviews the record. You must post a bond with good security for at least the judgment plus reasonable court costs. A late appeal may be allowed within 90 days for good cause. (W. Va. Code § 50-5-12; Rule 18, Rules of Civil Procedure for Magistrate Courts.)
west-virginia.sc_link_label: Rules of Civil Procedure for Magistrate Courts (Rule 18) | West Virginia Judiciary
west-virginia.sc_link2_label: W. Va. Code § 50-5-12 (Magistrate Court Appeals) | WV Legislature
west-virginia.gen_court: West Virginia Intermediate Court of Appeals
west-virginia.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days from the final order to file a notice of appeal. The case goes to the West Virginia Intermediate Court of Appeals, which reviews the record for legal errors. (West Virginia Rules of Appellate Procedure.)

wisconsin.sc_court: circuit judge or Court of Appeals
wisconsin.sc_text: There are two tracks. If a circuit court commissioner decided your small-claims case, you can demand a new trial (de novo) before a circuit judge: 10 days from the oral decision, or 15 days from the mailing of the written decision. The new trial covers all issues. If a circuit court judge decided the case, you appeal to the Court of Appeals: 45 days if written notice of entry was given within 21 days of the judgment, otherwise 90 days. There is no appeal from a default judgment — ask the court to reopen it instead. Eviction cases: 15 days. (Wis. Stat. §§ 799.207, 799.30, 799.29(1)(a), 799.44, 808.04.)
wisconsin.sc_link_label: Wis. Stat. § 799.29–799.30 (Small Claims Appeals) | Wisconsin Legislature
wisconsin.sc_link2_label: Wis. Stat. § 799.207 (Trial De Novo) | Wisconsin Legislature
wisconsin.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 45 days from entry of a final judgment to appeal to the Wisconsin Court of Appeals if written notice of entry was given within 21 days of the judgment — otherwise 90 days. The court reviews the record for legal errors. (Wis. Stat. § 808.04(1).)
wisconsin.gen_link_label: Wis. Stat. § 808.04 (Time for Appeal) | Wisconsin Legislature

wyoming.sc_text: You have 30 days from issuance of the judgment to file a notice of appeal to the district court. The district court decides questions of law only — it does not re-try the case and does not review whether the evidence was sufficient. Ask the clerk for the current fee. (Wyoming Rules of Appellate Procedure; W.R.A.P. 4(a).)
wyoming.gen_text: In other civil cases, you have 30 days from the date of the final judgment or order to file a notice of appeal with the district court, appealing to the Wyoming Supreme Court. The court reviews the record for legal errors.
wyoming.gen_link_label: Instructions on Filing a Notice of Appeal | Wyoming Judicial Branch
